rv.q: Feraud and director Tatiana Pandiani’s pacing is strong and lively; behind all the mayhem is a steady progression of moving toward the climax.
The fine ensemble helps make someone spectacular something worthwhile.
Not everybody will care to be reminded of their own grief, of course, but someone spectacular is an honest, sometimes touching study in life and loss.

cn.t: Critics find this real-time grief support group drama affecting and watchable, praising its fresh twist on loss and human connection, though reception remains moderately positive rather than rapturous.

vr.q: What I found unexpected about this play was just how funny a lot of the dialogue was.
